title: Southside
label: Unconfirmed

type.basis: Evidence specimen; South London's answer to an East London-centred scene, on Alias's Southside Riddim.

sound.text: Dan Hancox in the Guardian calls it 'so grimey'. Producer Alias left off his usual audio logo, reportedly fearing east London DJs would shut it down.
Mixmag (2018) calls it perhaps the most ostentatious example of grime's neighbourhood pride.

context.text: Written in response to south-versus-east London rivalry in early-2000s grime (Mixmag, 2018).
Complex (2014) lists the 'Southside' video as a 2005 Channel U anthem representing south London, paired with B.M.D.'s north London 'North Weezee'.
The Guardian piece argues that Channel U all-star videos put faces to voices and were early steps in grime's move towards pop.

rels.other: Alias (also producer of 'Gladiator', researched in batch C)

uncertainty: No label, catalogue number or physical format found; the 2005 date comes from Mixmag and Complex and may refer to the video or Channel U broadcast, not a commercial release. The Guardian article was read through an inkl syndication page with no visible date; internal references suggest c. 2017.
tracklist: All-star posse cut with verses from 15 south London MCs, each representing a crew, area or postcode (Mixmag, 2018; Guardian). Complex (2014) says Bashy and Asher D appear on it or on B.M.D.'s 'North Weezee'; it does not say which.
